v.why: With edge 4 absent, node 3 depends only on edges 3 and 5, so removing edge 3 risks disconnecting or severely bottlenecking the output (e.g. -78/-66/-37 when edges 4 and 5 are both none).
With edge 5 absent, removing the direct edge 0->3 leaves only the path through edge 4, or no path at all, which causes large consistent accuracy drops.
Without the direct edge 0->3, information must flow through node 1 or node 2, so cutting edge 0 often disconnects the cell (e.g. -78/-67/-23).
Removing a parameter-free skip on edge 0 in skip-heavy cells breaks the degenerate all-identity collapse, whereas removing a convolution loses capacity.
Deleting a skip on edge 5 in skip-dominated cells gives large gains (+42/+37/+8), while deleting a conv on edge 5 consistently hurts.
Adding another identity path to output in a cell already full of skips worsens the skip collapse (-28/-23/-2), while in conv cells the residual skip helps.
Adding a 3x3 conv to a skip-heavy cell supplies badly needed learnable capacity, giving far larger gains than in already conv-rich cells.
When downstream edges are parameter-free skips, a conv on edge 0 adds most of the cell's learnable computation (gains of +43 to +49 on CIFAR-10), unlike in conv-dominated cells.
Pooling-only cells have no learnable parameters, so adding a 3x3 conv on edge 5 yields very large improvements (+38/+41/+8) compared with conv-based parents.
In skip-based cells a conv on the internal edge 1->2 adds rare learnable depth (+5/+14/+10), whereas in conv-rich cells it is redundant and near-neutral.

raw:
Hypotheses were picked using two patterns in the 100 experiments:

- **Disconnection:** removing an edge can cut every path from input to output. Accuracy then collapses by about 40–79 points (experiments 4, 8, 33, 34).
- **Skip/pool collapse:** in parent cells that are mostly skip_connect or avg_pool_3x3, adding a convolution or removing a parameter-free edge gives very large gains. In convolution-rich parents, the same edits give small changes.
